interest: Shows rumors, relayed via FDR aide Howe, of a secret Cuban naval-base sale to Japan under President Machado.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.34537/1 and 894.34537/2) contains confidential correspondence from February and March 1934 between Secret Service Chief W. H. Moran of the Treasury Department and Under Secretary of State William Phillips regarding reports of a secret Japanese naval base in Cuba. The information originated from Mrs. Gail Hall de Montejo, an American woman residing in Camagüey married to a Cuban national, who alleged that corrupt officials during the regime of Cuban President Gerardo Machado had secretly sold naval base rights to Japan in violation of the Platt Amendment. Initiated at the suggestion of presidential advisor Colonel Louis McHenry Howe, the correspondence details local revolutionary figures in Camagüey (Dr. Louis Loasses and Paco Miranda), anti-Machado revolutionary intrigue, A.B.C. arms trafficking, and strict postal censorship in Cuba, while the State Department monitored and returned the transmitted materials.

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting an intelligence report from informant Gail Hall de Montejo to Under Secretary of State William Phillips.
subfiles.summary: Moran forwards Phillips a follow-up letter from Gail Hall de Montejo alleging a secret Japanese naval base deal in Cuba.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to William Phillips transmitting follow-up letter from Gail Hall de Montejo

subfiles.about: Informant letter identifying Cuban contacts with knowledge of the alleged Japanese naval base sale and offering intelligence on revolutionary arms smuggling.
subfiles.summary: Montejo names sources in Camagüey on Cuba's secret naval-base sale to Japan under Machado, and offers intel on A.B.C. revolutionary arms, asking strict secrecy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Gail Hall de Montejo to W. H. Moran regarding Japanese naval base rumors and Cuban revolutionaries

subfiles.about: Cover letter returning Gail Hall de Montejo's February 26 letter to the Secret Service Division after review.
subfiles.summary: Phillips thanks Moran for the Montejo letter on a Japanese naval base rumor in Cuba, returning the enclosure.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to W. H. Moran returning enclosure from Gail Hall de Montejo

subfiles.about: Confidential letter transmitting Mrs. de Montejo's initial report on a Japanese naval base in Cuba to Under Secretary Phillips at the recommendation of Colonel Louis Howe.
subfiles.summary: Moran forwards Montejo's first letter on a Japanese naval base rumor in Cuba, sent informally at Col. Howe's suggestion.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to William Phillips forwarding report of Japanese naval base in Cuba

subfiles.about: Acknowledgement from Secret Service Chief Moran commending Gail Hall de Montejo for reporting alleged Japanese naval base negotiations in Cuba.
subfiles.summary: Moran thanks Montejo for alerting his office to the rumored Japanese naval base in Cuba, inviting further information.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. H. Moran to Gail Hall de Montejo acknowledging report on Japanese naval base

subfiles.about: Initial report from Gail Hall de Montejo alerting the U.S. Secret Service to an alleged secret purchase of naval base rights in Cuba by Japan.
subfiles.summary: Montejo reports a secret Machado-era sale of a Cuban naval base site to Japan, warning it violates the Platt Amendment, and offers to gather more details.
subfiles.title: Letter from Gail Hall de Montejo to Secret Service Department reporting alleged Japanese naval base in Cuba

subfiles.about: Letter from Under Secretary Phillips returning Mrs. de Montejo's initial letter to Chief Moran and expressing interest in subsequent reports.
subfiles.summary: Phillips returns Montejo's letter on the Japanese naval-base rumor in Cuba, welcoming any further information she can provide.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to W. H. Moran returning Gail Hall de Montejo's initial letter
